surfaceRasters.name: LOLA permanently shadowed regions
surfaceRasters.description: All 1,531 regions larger than 1 km² from the Barker et al. south-pole release. The overview samples the modeled boundaries at 160 m. Use Point Probe to inspect a mapped region and select its original boundary. Zoom in to see detailed outlines. Permanent shadow is a model result from LOLA topography, independent of the simulation clock. Smaller regions and locations beyond the release footprint are unclassified by this layer.

surfaceRasters.name: Diviner summer maximum temperature
surfaceRasters.description: Maximum of south-polar summer bolometric brightness temperature bins from LRO Diviner observations, July 2009–February 2019. Fixed climatology, independent of the simulation clock. Transparent areas have no valid observations. Display saturates above 350 K; the probe preserves source values. Spatial sampling is 240 m. Geolocation and the instrument footprint limit site-scale interpretation.

surfaceRasters.name: Mini-RF south-pole δCPR mosaic
surfaceRasters.description: Regional LRO Mini-RF monostatic S-band mosaic south of 80°S. Fassett et al. adjusted the measured circular polarization ratio for local incidence angle, with a 0.42 offset for the 49° reference. Transparent areas are coverage gaps, including Shackleton’s center. The color scale is centered at 0.42 and clips below 0.20 and above 0.80. Point Probe reads the archived 90 m values. Radar scattering alone cannot identify ice.

surfaceRasters.name: Mini-RF bistatic CPR · Haworth
surfaceRasters.description: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Mini-RF X-band acquisition on 2022-12-19. The Earth-based DSS-13 transmitter illuminated the Moon and Mini-RF received the echoes from orbit. CPR varies with the viewing geometry and surface scattering, including roughness. Ice identification requires separate evidence. Transparent areas have no valid return in this swath. The color scale saturates above 1.8; readings retain the archived values.
